title: sydcli config
description: User configuration for sydcli, read from ~/.sydcli/config.json at startup. All fields are optional; anything omitted falls back to a built-in default.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor autocomplete/validation.

model.description: Model id active at startup. When omitted, the chosen provider's default model is used.

autoApprove.description: When true, file edits/writes apply without the per-change approval popup. Off is safer (each write asks first).

mcpServers.description: MCP servers to connect at startup. Each key is a short server name that also namespaces the server's tools (as <name>__<tool>). Give a stdio server a `command`, or an HTTP server a `url` — not both.

additionalProperties.description: One MCP server. Either a stdio (subprocess) server via `command`, or an HTTP/SSE server via `url`.

transport.description: Transport kind. Optional — inferred as stdio when `command` is set, http when `url` is set.

command.description: Stdio server: the executable to spawn (e.g. "npx").

args.description: Stdio server: arguments passed to the command.

env.description: Stdio server: extra environment variables for the subprocess. Values may reference the shell environment with ${VAR} so secrets stay out of this file.

cwd.description: Stdio server: working directory for the subprocess.

headers.description: HTTP/SSE server: extra request headers (e.g. Authorization). Values may reference the shell environment with ${VAR} so secrets stay out of this file.

auth.description: HTTP/SSE server: set to "oauth" to authenticate via an interactive browser login (run /mcp login <name> in syd) instead of a static token. Omit for header/no auth.

trust.description: "prompt" (default): every tool call from this server asks for approval first. "trusted": its tools run without a prompt.
